chains.description: Canonical industry chain for discrete and integrated semiconductor devices that switch, convert, and control electrical power.
chains.scope: Covers silicon MOSFETs, silicon-carbide power devices, gallium-nitride power devices, and their device-level manufacturing routes for power conversion applications.
exclusions: Power-supply equipment, converter assemblies, and application-specific power architectures remain owned by power_electronics_power_supply_equipment.
Signal-processing, radio-frequency, memory, and logic semiconductors remain owned by their respective semiconductor chains.

chains.description: Equipment and factory systems used to execute, control, and support front-end semiconductor wafer manufacturing.
chains.scope: Covers wafer-fabrication process equipment, inspection and metrology, wafer automation, vacuum and process delivery, and fab utility systems.
exclusions: Semiconductor materials are owned by the semiconductor materials chain.
Semiconductor packaging and test equipment are owned by the packaging and test chain, except wafer_thinning is temporarily canonical here and may be referenced by advanced packaging.

chains.description: Canonical industry chain for electrical interconnect products and passive components that route, join, filter, and condition power or signals.
chains.scope: Covers power cables, busbars and busways, high-current and HVDC connectors, flexible copper links, magnetic components, capacitors, and related manufacturing processes.
exclusions: Active power semiconductor devices remain owned by power_semiconductors.
Complete power-conversion and distribution equipment remains owned by power_electronics_power_supply_equipment.
aliases: 印制电路板被动元件与连接互连

chains.description: Canonical infrastructure chain for data-center facilities, thermal systems, integrated delivery, commissioning, and operations.
chains.scope: Covers modular data-center systems, liquid-cooling equipment and loops, facility integration, DCIM platforms, electrical design, EPC, commissioning, certification, and facility operations.
exclusions: Generic utility generation, grid equipment, and power-conversion products remain owned by their primary energy chains.
Compute chips, servers, storage, and network equipment remain owned by their respective information-technology and semiconductor chains.
aliases: 云与数据中心基础设施

chains.description: Canonical industry chain for operational, engineering, monitoring, optimization, and predictive software used in industrial and infrastructure systems.
chains.scope: Covers electrical and facility monitoring platforms, building management software, thermal control, fault prediction, compute-energy scheduling, and carbon, energy, and cost optimization software.
exclusions: Physical power, grid, cooling, and data-center facility equipment remains owned by the corresponding equipment or infrastructure chain.
Generic operating systems, databases, and cybersecurity platforms remain owned by their primary foundational-software chains.

chains.description: A primarily system-architecture decomposition of humanoid robots spanning embodied intelligence, control, sensing, compute, actuation, body, and energy subsystems, with one explicit supplementary lifecycle and value-chain family.
chains.scope: Covers robot-specific models and software, integrated sensing and control modules, reusable electromechanical components, complete humanoid robots, and their manufacturing, test, operations, and scenario integration. Under the approved mixed-template rule, humanoid_manufacturing_test_integration supplements the primary system architecture with lifecycle coverage.
exclusions: General-purpose AI foundation models remain owned by their primary AI chain; this chain covers robot-adapted embodied models and inference.
General semiconductor chips remain owned by semiconductor chains; this chain covers robot-selected compute components and integrated modules.

Generic battery cells, battery management systems, and battery materials remain owned by power_batteries_battery_materials; this chain covers humanoid-specific selection, integration, and control requirements.
General industrial robots, machine tools, and factory automation remain owned by their primary equipment chains unless humanoid-specific.
aliases: 人形机器人与具身智能

chains.chain_name: New Power System and Smart Grid
chains.description: Canonical infrastructure chain for connecting, transforming, switching, protecting, monitoring, and maintaining power flows across modern grids.
chains.scope: Covers grid-connection engineering, substations, transformers, switchgear, relay protection, power-quality systems, DC breakers, and DC protection systems.
exclusions: Power generation equipment and energy procurement services remain owned by power_generation_energy_equipment.
Data-center internal UPS, rectification, rack distribution, and server power equipment remain owned by power_electronics_power_supply_equipment.
aliases: 新型电力系统与智能电网

chains.description: Canonical industry chain for generation systems, power-supply services, distributed energy, microgrids, and generation-based resilience.
chains.scope: Covers grid and nuclear supply services, renewable procurement services, distributed generation, gas turbines, microgrids, diesel and gas backup generation, and black-start generation services.
exclusions: Grid connection, substations, transformation, and protection remain owned by new_power_system_smart_grid.
Fuel-cell and battery storage technologies remain owned by hydrogen_fuel_cells and power_batteries_battery_materials respectively.

chains.chain_name: Power Electronics and Power Supply Equipment
chains.description: Canonical industry chain for power conversion, transfer, distribution, regulation, and control equipment from facility input through server-board delivery.
chains.scope: Covers UPS equipment, transfer switches, rectifiers and inverters, HVDC systems, DC buses, power distribution units, power shelves, server power supplies, AC-DC and DC-DC modules, voltage regulators, and power controllers.
exclusions: Power semiconductor devices and passive interconnect components remain owned by their respective semiconductor and interconnect chains.
Utility-grid substations, transformers, switchgear, and grid protection remain owned by new_power_system_smart_grid.

chains.description: Application-chain view of the electrical, thermal, software, engineering, and operational dependencies required to power high-density AI data centers.
chains.scope: Covers capacity planning, resilient energy supply, grid access, backup power, UPS and DC conversion, room and rack distribution, server-board power, liquid cooling, energy-management software, and facility delivery and operations for AI data centers.
exclusions: Canonical product, service, technology, company, and evidence ownership remains on the referenced non-application industry-chain nodes.
Compute accelerators, servers, networking, storage, and AI software workloads are outside this power-application chain except where they define power or cooling requirements.
aliases: AI Compute Power and Cooling Chain
AI数据中心电力基础设施

chains.description: Primary canonical ownership skeleton for power-battery cells, battery management platforms, pack and system integration, and battery materials across the manufacturing value chain.
chains.scope: This skeleton establishes canonical ownership for generic high-specific-energy power-battery cells and battery management system platforms. Later expansion may add cell manufacturing, pack integration, recycling, and battery-material process families without changing application-chain ownership.
exclusions: Humanoid-specific cell selection, BMS integration, robot battery packs, and robot power controls remain owned by humanoid_robots_embodied_intelligence.
Stationary energy-storage systems and grid integration remain owned by their primary energy-storage and power-system chains.
Vehicle-specific battery installation and vehicle energy management remain owned by intelligent-vehicle chains; generic battery products remain canonical here.

chains.description: Canonical technology-route chain for hydrogen conversion and fuel-cell systems used in stationary, mobile, and industrial energy applications.
chains.scope: Covers stationary fuel-cell backup systems and their fuel-cell technology route, balance-of-plant integration, and application-neutral product ownership.
exclusions: Hydrogen production, transport, and storage infrastructure outside the fuel-cell system boundary remains owned by dedicated hydrogen supply chains when introduced.
Application-specific backup-power sizing, redundancy, and facility integration remain owned by the relevant application chain.
